deep.reconstruction:
Setting. 𝒜 is a von Neumann algebra on H with a faithful normal semifinite trace T (also written Tr). 𝔟 is a two-sided ideal of 𝒜, essentially the τ-measurable or τ-compact-type elements. 𝔟⁺ is its positive part and P(𝒜) is the projection lattice. For A ∈ 𝔟⁺, φ_A is the decreasing rearrangement of A with respect to T: the inverse function of t ↦ T(spectral projection of A on ]s,∞[). φ_A⁻ is its left-continuous version. The earlier formula (4) treats the commutative case (N = 1).

Prop 6 (minimax formula). For A ∈ 𝔟⁺:
φ_A⁻(t) = inf over E ∈ P(𝒜) with T(E) < t of sup over x ∈ (1−E)H, ||x|| ≤ 1, of (Ax, x)
= inf over the same E of ||(1−E)A(1−E)||.
The strict inequality T(E) < t is what produces the left-continuous version. Fack–Kosaki use T(E) ≤ t and get the right-continuous μ_t.

Proof sketch, as far as legible. Take 𝔠, apparently a maximal abelian subalgebra containing A; the transcription's '𝔠 = 𝓛(H)' looks wrong. Restricting the infimum to projections E in 𝔠 reduces to the commutative case (formula (4), N = 1). This gives equality with φ_A⁻(t) for E ∈ 𝔠, hence one inequality for the infimum over all E. The reverse inequality is then argued for arbitrary E ∈ P(𝒜).

Corollary 1. For A ∈ 𝔟 and |A| = √(A*A):
φ_{|A|}⁻(t) = inf over T(E) < t of sup over x ∈ (1−E)H, ||x|| ≤ 1, of ||Ax|| = inf over T(E) < t of ||A(1−E)||.

Corollary 2. For A ∈ 𝔟 and B ∈ 𝒜: φ_{|BA|} ≤ ||B|| φ_{|A|} and φ_{|AB|} ≤ ||B|| φ_{|A|}.

Corollary 3. φ_A is continuous, apparently in A, for A ∈ 𝔟⁺.

Corollary 4. The functions A ↦ φ_{|A|}⁻(t) on 𝔟 form a family defining, or continuous for, the natural topology of 𝔟. The text is only partly legible.

Corollary 5 (left margin). An inequality of the form φ_{|A+B|}(s+t) ≤ φ_{|A|}(s) + φ_{|B|}(t), i.e. the Ky Fan-type subadditivity.

Purpose. This is the systematic theory of generalized singular numbers (s-numbers) in semifinite von Neumann algebras. It prepares Prop 7 (φ_{|A|} = φ_{|A*|}, via T(RS) = T(SR) and moments) and the Fuglede–Kadison-type determinant Δ(A) = exp ∫₀^{T(1)} log φ_{|A|}, treated on the next page.

Modern counterpart. These are Fack–Kosaki 1986, Prop. 2.2 and Lemma 2.5: μ_t(x) = inf{||x(1−e)|| : τ(e) ≤ t}, μ_t(axb) ≤ ||a|| ||b|| μ_t(x), μ_{s+t}(x+y) ≤ μ_s(x) + μ_t(y), and continuity. Grothendieck published related material in Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'.
errors: The second inequality of Corollary 2, φ_{|AB|} ≤ ||B|| φ_{|A|}, does not follow directly from formula (6). (6) controls ||AB(1−E)||, not ||A(1−F)||. The natural proof passes to adjoints: |AB| ~ |B*A*|. That uses φ_{|X|} = φ_{|X*|}, which is only proved on the next page as Prop 7. So the logical order on this page is off. Alternatively a direct kernel/support-projection argument is needed, and it is not given.
In (5)/(6) the infimum is written over E ∈ P(A). It should be P(𝒜), the projections of the algebra; this is a notational slip.
The proof of the reverse inequality in Prop 6 is only sketched; the general E ∉ 𝔠 case is not legibly argued.
Corollaries 3–5 are stated without proof. Corollary 5 is only a marginal reminder.

ideas.what: Minimax (Courant–Fischer type) formula for the rearrangement / generalized singular numbers of an operator in a von Neumann algebra with trace: φ_A(t) = inf{||A(1−E)|| : T(E) < t}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fack–Kosaki (1986), with antecedents in Murray–von Neumann, Ovchinnikov (1970) and Grothendieck's Bourbaki exposé (1955)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955) treats rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with trace; whether this exact minimax formula appears there is unsure

ideas.what: Ky Fan inequality μ_{s+t}(A+B) ≤ μ_s(A) + μ_t(B) and continuity of A ↦ μ_t(A)
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan-type subadditivity of generalized singular values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ky Fan (matrices / compact operators); Fack–Kosaki (von Neumann algebras)

ideas.what: Context (next page): μ_{|A|} = μ_{|A*|} via trace property and moments; determinant Δ(A) = exp ∫ log φ_{|A|}
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant expressed through generalized s-numbers

missed.claim: By 1953 Grothendieck had the minimax characterization of generalized singular numbers in semifinite von Neumann algebras, with the standard corollaries (ideal property, continuity, a Ky Fan-type inequality). The standard modern reference is Fack–Kosaki 1986. His published Bourbaki exposé (1955) on rearrangements is cited in that literature, so the priority is partly on record. The detailed minimax statement in these notes is an earlier, fuller version.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only. The mathematics is now standard in noncommutative integration (Fack–Kosaki, Dodds–Dodds–de Pagter); no new content for a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: These are early, correct versions of now-standard facts on generalized s-numbers. They are closely tied to Grothendieck's own published Bourbaki exposé 113 on rearrangements in von Neumann algebras, which the field knows and cites. There is no new mathematics or unmade connection.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit 𝔠 = 𝓛(H)' is likely wrong. The struck/handwritten text seems to define 𝔠 as a (maximal) abelian subalgebra of 𝔟 or 𝒜 containing A, so that the commutative case (N = 1, formula (4)) applies.

In the proof line, the sign before φ_A^-(t) is a (heavily written) relation symbol, probably '≥' or '=', in 'inf ||(1−E)A||_∞ ⋯ φ_A^-(t)'. The second inequality '≥' is then asserted at the end of the proof.
'Corollaire 5' is written vertically in the left margin. It reads roughly 'Corollaire 5: φ_{|A+B|}(t+t') ≤ φ(...)+...', and the marginal 'pour |A| = √(A*A)' belongs to Corollaire 1.
In (6), the sup is presumably over unit vectors x ∈ (1−E)H; T(E) and Tr(E) denote the same trace.
